## Annual leave
Full-time employees receive 18 working days of annual leave per calendar year. Requests go through the staff portal and need manager approval before travel is booked. Unused days may roll over only up to five days into the next year. The People team answers questions about balance corrections. This paragraph defines the annual leave rule; it does not define contractor benefits.

# Security standard

## Multi-factor authentication
All staff must enable multi-factor authentication on the corporate identity account. Hardware security keys are preferred for privileged administrators. Recovery codes belong in the approved password manager, never in a shared chat room. The service desk can reset a lost factor only after an identity check. This rule covers corporate sign-in and does not specify personal device passwords.

## Access review
Application owners review production access every 90 days. They remove unneeded roles and record the review ticket in the access register. Emergency access expires after 24 hours unless a security lead approves an extension. The access register is the evidence for auditors. A review is required even if no role changed during the previous quarter.

## Incident reporting
A suspected security incident must be reported to the security duty channel within 30 minutes of discovery. The first report includes the time, affected service and observed symptom; it should avoid copying customer secrets. The security lead assigns severity and coordinates containment. Staff should preserve relevant evidence instead of deleting suspicious files.

## Data classification
Documents containing customer identifiers are classified Confidential. Confidential files may be shared only through the approved encrypted workspace with authorized recipients. Public materials can be posted externally after the owner approves them. A classification label follows the content when it is copied into a new document. The standard does not set a retention period for recordings.

cases.question: On which days are routine production deployments scheduled?
cases.answer: Routine production deployments are scheduled on Tuesday and Thursday between 10:00 and 16:00 local time.

citation_checks.content:
# Operations runbook

## Deployment window
Routine production deployments run on Tuesday and Thursday between 10:00 and 16:00 local time. The release owner posts a change ticket before starting and records the deployed version afterward. Emergency fixes outside that window need the on-call lead's approval. The window reduces handoff risk, but it does not remove the requirement for automated checks.

## Rollback
If the error rate exceeds five percent for ten consecutive minutes after a release, the release owner starts rollback. The owner restores the last known good image and posts an incident update. Database migrations need an explicit rollback plan in the change ticket because a container rollback alone may not restore schema compatibility. The on-call lead confirms service recovery.

The primary on-call engineer hands off at 09:00 every Monday. The handoff note lists open incidents, risky changes and dashboard links. The secondary engineer acknowledges the handoff within one hour. If the primary cannot respond, the secondary becomes incident commander until a lead assigns a replacement. ## Backup checks
PostgreSQL backups are checked every morning at 08:00. The daily check confirms the latest backup completed and that its checksum matches the stored manifest. A restore drill is run once each quarter in an isolated environment. The backup operator records failures in the operations ticket queue and pages on-call if two consecutive checks fail.

# Procurement guide

## Purchase approvals
Purchases above 5000 currency units require approval from the department head and Finance before an order is placed. Smaller purchases still need the cost center owner's approval. Splitting one order into several smaller orders to avoid the threshold is prohibited. The request includes the expected amount, business reason and proposed supplier.

## Vendor security review
Any supplier that will process customer data must complete a security review before contract signature. The requester submits the vendor questionnaire and a data flow summary to Security. Security records approval or conditions in the vendor register. The contract cannot substitute for this review, and the review must be repeated when processing scope changes substantially.

cases.question: What is the first human response target for priority-one support tickets?
cases.answer: A support agent confirms the impact and assigns an incident lead before proposing a fix.

citation_checks.content:
# Support playbook

## First response
Priority-one support tickets receive a first human response within 15 minutes. A support agent confirms the impact and assigns an incident lead before proposing a fix. Automated acknowledgements do not count as the human first response. The ticket timeline is the source of truth for measuring this target. Lower priority tickets use a different schedule not listed here.

## Escalation
If a priority-one issue remains unresolved after 60 minutes, the support lead escalates to the on-call engineering lead. The escalation includes the ticket ID, customer impact, mitigation tried and next update time. The engineering lead acknowledges within ten minutes. Support continues customer communication while engineering investigates the technical cause.
